title: El café de olla y el pan dulce en Coyoacán

dialogue.speaker: Sofía
dialogue.spanish: Oye, Luis, pues ¿pedimos dos cafés de olla aquí en la panadería antes de tomar el camión?
dialogue.english: Hey, Luis, well should we order two spiced pot coffees here at the bakery before taking the bus?

slang.actualMeaning: the city passenger bus (standard everyday word in Mexico)
slang.example: El camión al centro pasa cada diez minutos.

dialogue.speaker: Luis
dialogue.spanish: ¿Mande? Perdón, es que estaba contestando un mensaje del trabajo. Sí, buena idea, hace bastante frío hoy.
dialogue.english: Pardon? Sorry, I was replying to a work message. Yes, good idea, it's pretty cold today.

slang.actualMeaning: Pardon? / What did you say? (Polite Mexican way to ask someone to repeat)

dialogue.speaker: Sofía
dialogue.spanish: Bueno, también voy a llevar dos conchas de vainilla recién salidas del horno para desayunar en la oficina.
dialogue.english: Well, I'm also going to get two vanilla sweet breads fresh out of the oven for breakfast at the office.

dialogue.speaker: Luis
dialogue.spanish: ¡Qué rico huele! O sea, ¿cuánto es por los dos cafés y el pan dulce?
dialogue.english: It smells so good! I mean, how much is it for the two coffees and the sweet bread?

dialogue.speaker: Sofía
dialogue.spanish: La señorita de la caja dice que son sesenta y cinco pesos en total por todo.
dialogue.english: The cashier lady says it's sixty-five pesos total for everything.

dialogue.speaker: Luis
dialogue.spanish: Yo invito hoy, Sofía. Pero apúrate porque nuestro camión pasa en ocho minutos por la avenida.
dialogue.english: It's my treat today, Sofía. But hurry up because our bus comes down the avenue in eight minutes.

slang.actualMeaning: It's my treat / I'm paying for both of us
slang.example: Guarda tu cartera, hoy yo invito los tacos.

questions.question: Why does Luis say '¿Mande?' when Sofía first speaks to him?
options: He was replying to a work message on his phone and didn't catch what she said
He forgot his wallet at home
The bakery music is too loud
questions.explanation: Luis replies: '¿Mande? Perdón, es que estaba contestando un mensaje del trabajo.'

questions.question: What does Sofía pick up to eat at the office, and how much is the entire order?
options: Two vanilla conchas (sweet breads), and the total with coffees is 65 pesos
Three churros, and the total is 50 pesos
One ham sandwich, and the total is 45 pesos
Two tamales, and the total is 30 pesos
questions.explanation: Sofía gets 'dos conchas de vainilla' and says 'son sesenta y cinco pesos en total por todo.'

questions.question: Why does Luis tell Sofía to hurry up at the end?
options: Their bus ('el camión') comes down the avenue in 8 minutes
The bakery is about to close
It is starting to rain outside
Their boss just called on his cell phone
questions.explanation: Luis says: 'apúrate porque nuestro camión pasa en ocho minutos por la avenida.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: In Mexican Spanish, what do '¿Mande?', 'el camión', and 'Yo invito' mean?
options: '¿Mande?' = Pardon?; 'el camión' = the city bus; 'Yo invito' = It's my treat
'¿Mande?' = Send it; 'el camión' = the subway; 'Yo invito' = Come to my party
'¿Mande?' = Hurry up; 'el camión' = the bicycle; 'Yo invito' = Let's split it
'¿Mande?' = Excuse me; 'el camión' = the taxi; 'Yo invito' = You pay today
questions.explanation: In Mexico, '¿Mande?' is the polite way to say 'Pardon?', 'el camión' is the passenger bus, and 'Yo invito' means 'My treat!'
